## Finding

For `unsigned *const p = init (&(unsigned){0});` the compiler initializes the compound literal
before the call of `init` and a second time after it. The second initialization overwrites the 42
that `init` stores through the pointer, so `*p` is 0. The reporter shows this in the code for z80
and names r16747 as the revision that introduced it. The cause is in `gatherAutoInit`, which every
port uses. For mcs51 the regression test shows the defect on r17176.

## Cause

`gatherAutoInit` in `src/SDCCast.c` loops over the symbols of a block and builds the code for
their initializers. When an initializer has a compound literal, the loop body appends the
temporary symbol of the literal to the same chain and initializes it with a recursive call, before
the declaration that uses it. The loop later processes the symbol that it appended. A `constexpr`
symbol keeps `sym->ival` for evaluation at compile time, and a compound literal with a constant
initializer is implicitly `constexpr`, so the loop initializes it a second time.

## Fix

`gatherAutoInit` finds the last symbol of the chain before the loop starts, and the loop ends
after that symbol. The patch attached to the ticket makes the same change to `gatherAutoInit`.

## Verification

`support/regression/tests/bug-4248.c` has the ticket's example and asserts that `*p` is 42. Without
the patch the test fails on r17176 for all six mcs51 variants. The test in the ticket's patch also
has struct and union literals and several declarations.
